records.title: Aviation Medicine. Monthly Progress Report No. 6.
records.note: Status through July 24, 1942. Same project and altitude as the August 31 progress report, with unverified participant overlap and different reported age limits. A symptom-triggered chamber descent could end tests for other occupants. The source reports repeated flights with no individual data.

observations.protocol: Standardized group flights with repeated attendance to 35,000 ft. The exposure ended when symptom severity in one person necessitated descent. Individual activity, gas delivery and flight linkage are not documented.
observations.outcome_window: Across the reported exploratory flights through July 24. A common delayed-symptom window was unavailable.
observations.locator: Report 6, section 4 (NLM item 101085500X267, image 496)
observations.note: Exact complement of the two participants the authors explicitly say had no bends. Both had only one flight.

observations.note: Described as syncopal-like reactions with peripheral circulatory collapse, often alongside other symptoms.

records.followup_note: Pain, local tenderness or swelling, orthostatic hypotension, leukocytosis, cough and fatigue were described from hours to several days after flight. No cases or risk sets were specified for those delayed symptoms.

records.title: Aviation Medicine. Bi-Monthly Progress Report No. 13.
records.note: The August progress report gives 102 entrants, 80 seven-flight completers and 560 man-flights among those completers. The July minutes give 78 in the seven-flight tables and 83 in a symptom graph and the discussion. These are named source scopes. Individual correspondence and the reasons the three totals differ were not reported.

observations.protocol: Four flights at 38,000 ft using the Subcommittee protocol and three at 35,000 ft, using five deep knee bends every three minutes.
observations.outcome_window: Across the completed sequence as reported in August 1943.
observations.locator: Report 13, opening paragraph (NLM item 101085500X267, image 510)
observations.note: Attendance endpoint. Exact pattern and number of flights among the other 22 entrants were not supplied.

records.title: Aviation Medicine. Bi-Monthly Progress Report No. 14.
records.note: The October update mentions 80 people in the preselection validation and 95 classified people with body density measurements. It also reports completion of a small severe exercise series at 30,000 and 35,000 ft, without outcomes or a denominator in this report. It gives no participant linkage.

records.title: Report on the 90-minute altitude preselection test.
records.locator: Ninth CAM meeting, section III item 2, Table 4, printed p. 223 (PDF p. 222)
records.note: Fifty-six original percentage cells from the same seven-flight 78-person analysis already registered in v1.147–v1.149. Two classification methods are alternative descriptions of these participants. The 38,000-ft fourth columns total 116.7% and 87.2% as printed. Retain the discrepant cells and separate 83-person symptom-analysis scope.
